title: CMINNs: Compartment model informed neural networks — Unlocking drug dynamics

content.abstract_summary: Proposes CMINNs (Compartment Model Informed Neural Networks), a physics-informed neural network framework that embeds fractional calculus and time-varying parameters into compartmental PK/PD models. Uses PINNs and fractional PINNs (fPINNs) to simultaneously model anomalous diffusion, drug resistance, tolerance, and time-varying PK parameters within systems of two (fractional) ODEs. Demonstrates on cancer pharmacodynamics with multi-dose regimens. From the Karniadakis group at Brown University — the leading academic group in physics-informed ML for scientific computing.
key_findings: CMINNs integrate fractional calculus (anomalous diffusion, drug trapping/escape in heterogeneous tissues) with compartmental PK/PD models using PINNs — extends standard integer-order compartmental models to capture non-Fickian diffusion phenomena

Achieves modeling of drug resistance, persistence, tolerance, and absorption anomalies within a system of just 2 (fractional) ODEs — demonstrates that physics-constrained neural approaches can uncover dynamics inaccessible to standard compartmental forms
Time-varying parameters (piecewise constant or continuous) are learned by the neural network, enabling adaptation to changing patient physiology during treatment
Multi-dose administration modeled explicitly — relevant to oncology protocols (doxorubicin) where dose-response history affects cell death dynamics
Karniadakis group (Brown/NIH) involvement signals connection to the broader SciML ecosystem and potential for tool integration
limitations: Demonstrated on synthetic/simulated cancer PD data — clinical validation on real patient data is not presented
Fractional differential equations are computationally more expensive than integer ODEs and have less established estimation theory in pharmacometrics
Identifiability of fractional order parameter and neural components is not addressed — adding fractional calculus increases the identifiability challenge beyond standard hybrid models

extracted_claims.text: CMINNs uncover different drug-effect dynamics, providing new insights into absorption rates, anomalous diffusion, drug resistance, persistence, and pharmacokinetic tolerance, all within a system of just two (fractional) ODEs with explainable results.

gaps_addressed: Fills the PINN-based hybrid category in M1.1 architecture taxonomy — CMINNs represent the physics-informed approach (constraints from known ODE structure) rather than the data-driven neural ODE approach, giving a third architectural option alongside serial and embedded hybrids

The fractional calculus extension is directly relevant to M4.1 — physics-constrained generative models where the physics constraint is a fractional ODE rather than an integer ODE; this is an underexplored area the WG could carve out
